subject: repeated measures for a longitudinal design

messages.author: 6812af56a5ebeb25
messages.subject: repeated measures for a longitudinal design
parts:
Hi all,
Another new ez user here. My experiment is a little different than the
examples that I've been able to find online - it's a longitudinal
study - so I wanted to check that I've got this right before
proceeding.

I measured a dependent variable (phytoplankton) in 48 aquaria at 10
different time points. This was a 2x2x2 factorial design, so I have 3
between-subject factors, each with two levels. Time is a within-
subject factor, since each tank was measured at all 10 time points.
The design is fully balanced and the time points were equally spaced.
I'm interested in finding out whether my 3 factorial treatments
affected phytoplankton concentration.

dv = phytoplankton concentration
wid = tank
within = time
between = my 3 factorial treatments

In addition to main effects, I'm interested in knowing whether there
were two-way interactions between any of my 3 factorial treatments
(factor1*factor2, factor1*factor3, and/or factor 2*factor3), but I'd
rather avoid the three-way interactions for the sake of simplicity.
Furthermore, I expect phytoplankton concentration to change over time,
so that main effect and interactions between time and my factorial
treatments are interesting to me. I certainly don't want to deal with
the four-way interaction: factor1*factor2*factor3*time. Can anyone
tell me how to get these two-way interactions without the three- and
four-way interactions?

Thank you for your time.
Julia

messages.author: cb25d91fd630a4e5
messages.subject: Re: [ez4r] repeated measures for a longitudinal design
parts:
Hi Julia,

If you want to do an ANOVA, you should be able to do simply:

my_anova = ezANOVA(
data = my_data
, dv = .(phyto_con)
, wid = .(tank)
, within = .(time)
, between = .(v1,v2,v3)
)
print(my_anova)

Where I assume your data are in a data frame called my_data, which is
in "long" format with columns named phyto_con (containing
phytoplankton concentration values), tank (containing tank
identifiers), time (containing time identifiers), and three columns
named v1-v3, each containing identifiers for the different
between-groups treatments. Obviously if your data have different
column names, just replace the text above with the appropriate names.
If your data are in a different format, look at the reshape2 package
for how to reshape to long data format (ez and most R analysis
functions prefer long data format).

Cheers,

Mike

messages.author: 265b547d9e4946a9
messages.subject: Re: repeated measures for a longitudinal design
parts:
As it is a balanced design there is no much point in specifying a
model without three-way interactions as the interactions and main
effects are orthogonal. You can misinterpret the results if you omit
the interactions altogether. If you want to fit the model without
three-way interactions it would be easier perhaps using the lme4 or
nlme multilevel/linear mixed model packages directly. However, it is
important to check that the two-way model is a reasonable model.

library(nlme)

two-way only:

lme(phyto_con ~ (v1+v2+v3+time)^2, random=~1|tank/time, my_data)

three-way only:

lme(phyto_con ~ (v1+v2+v3+time)^3, random=~1|tank/time, my_data)

full factorial model:

lme(phyto_con ~ v1*v2*v3*time, random=~1|tank/time, my_data)

to compare the fit of the model with-way interactions only with the
model with three-way:

m2 <- lme(phyto_con ~ (v1+v2+v3+time)^2, random=~1|tank/time, my_data)
m3 <- lme(phyto_con ~ (v1+v2+v3+time)^3, random=~1|tank/time, my_data)

anova(m2, m3)


Thom

Thank you for the thorough and timely responses!

As a follow-up question, I received the following warnings when I ran
the analysis as Mike suggested:

Warning: Converting "tank" to factor for ANOVA. #
tank was coded as 1-48
Warning: "time" will be treated as numeric.
# time was coded as 1-10
Warning: "v1" will be treated as
numeric. # treatment 1 was coded as 1s
and 0s (for presence/absence)
Warning: "v2" will be treated as
numeric. # same as above
Warning: "v3" will be treated as
numeric. # same as above
Warning: There is at least one numeric within variable, therefore
aov() will be used for computation and no assumption checks will be
obtained.

How can I recode v1, v2, and v3 as factors? Also, I was expecting to
obtain a test of sphericity, which makes me think that time should not
be treated as numeric. Based on the graphs, though, the p-values that
I obtained seem reasonable.

Sorry for the newbie questions, and thank you again for your time.
Julia

messages.author: 0714839561195f1a
messages.subject: Re: [ez4r] Re: repeated measures for a longitudinal design

Julia,

You can convert something to a factor like:
df$v1 = factor(df$v1)
for some data frame df and variable v1. I think you want 'time' to be a
factor, in addition to your between variables.

Dan

messages.author: cb25d91fd630a4e5
messages.subject: Re: [ez4r] Re: repeated measures for a longitudinal design
parts:
When a variable simply has 2 levels, the ANOVA results won't differ
whether you treat it as numeric (0/1) or as a factor; differences may
arise when the variable has more than 2 levels. ezANOVA, however,
cannot compute sphericity tests if any within variables are numeric.

messages.author: 265b547d9e4946a9
messages.subject: Re: repeated measures for a longitudinal design
parts:
This is generally true - because the default contrasts in R are dummy
(treatment) coded. If you switch to effect (sum) coding it will not
necessarily be true (depending on what ANOVA commands are used). This
is a general point when fitting ANOVA models as GLMs in any package -
the choice of coding scheme can alter the interpretation of
coefficients (though not the overall model).

Thom
